source.title: What Visual Generators Need from Teachers: Rethinking Representation Alignment
source.authors: Yongcong Wang; Hingchin Chen; Mingyu Fan; Shuo Jiang; Teer Zhang; Yucong Sun; Zijia Wang; Yiming Lu; Chengchao Shen

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study refines and partly challenges representation-alignment assumptions: student-to-teacher feature recoverability stalls for deep teacher increments, and CKA ranks alignment placements in the reverse order from the proposed recoverability gap.
record.gate_note: The paper measures linear recovery of teacher features from a diffusion student's hidden states and compares representation-similarity criteria with alignment benefit. These bear on V4, V6 and V7, but do not test convergence across model scale or modalities as posed in V1 and V2. The many FID comparisons of alignment recipes and the other criteria in Table 1 (linear probing, LDS, gate ablation and gradient-based criteria) do not themselves measure the versions catalogued here and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Unaligned students' held-out linear recovery of independently pretrained teacher representations directly tests V4 and the incomplete-convergence component of V7. Placement-benefit correlations measure alignment utility, rather than metric dependence of convergence itself.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report bottom-up recovery with a deep-layer stall and argue that missing teacher content predicts alignment benefit better than existing similarity. They present RARE as a practical alignment recipe. The gap dynamics in R5–R6 belong to the selected-cell ablation, not main RARE.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies teacher-feature recoverability and alignment placement in diffusion generators, rather than measuring convergence among independently trained networks using the original sources' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The ranking depends on the criterion: at the 50K checkpoint the recoverability gap correlates positively with placement benefit while CKA correlates negatively; Gram similarity changes sign between 10K and later checkpoints. The paper also reports that the gap's usefulness depends on a shared normalization ceiling.

fits_no_version.finding: The recoverability gap predicts placement benefit positively, while readout R² and CKA predict it negatively; Gram similarity is unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Existing representational similarity need not predict the benefit of explicitly aligning a generator to a teacher.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit alignment reduces the selected cell's gap from 0.92 to 0.44 at 200K; it is 0.64 at 400K after release at 250K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher-directed training can induce partially persistent linear recoverability of teacher features.

record.problems: The authors note one training seed per main setting and restrict transfer studies to 100K endpoints in several settings. The linear-readout results measure only recoverability under the study's readout family; they do not establish general representational interchangeability or convergence across independently trained models.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2-9 and related figures report generator FID and other generation-quality metrics for alignment recipes, not representation convergence. Table 1's LDS, linear-probing, gate-ablation, gradient-cosine and first-order-utility results were omitted because they are not similarity measurements named by the claim versions. Detailed per-layer/per-block figure profiles beyond the explicit values in Sections 3.2 and 6.2 were not extracted.

untested.parts: No measured trend connecting increasing model scale or capability to increasing intermodel alignment; scale-transfer FID results do not establish that trend.
No paired image-caption representation comparison or joint vision-language capability trend.
No shared-feature or shared-subspace comparison across independently initialized copies of one architecture.
No functional substitution, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping. Readouts assess whitened rank-128 teacher targets under a particular linear regression family.
No identification of recurring interpretable features or circuits.

No direct demonstration that a convergence finding weakens or disappears under alternative similarity measures, inputs or out-of-distribution evaluation. Criterion correlations concern generation benefit.

No causal test of shared training data or objectives as explanations, or evidence distinguishing these from a common model of reality. The stall is established only within finite training budgets and the linear readout family.

record.verdict_notes: States for R1–R4 describe recoverability; absent deep recovery supports V7's incompleteness claim. A normalized recoverability gap is relative to a shared empirical ceiling, not the absolute fraction of all teacher information missing. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether independently trained models with differing architectures, objectives and data become more aligned as scale and capability increase.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language alignment trend is measured.
Does not compare training seeds for shared features or subspaces, or assess individual units or bases.

Tests linear readout of teacher features from a diffusion student's hidden states, not stitching, relative representations, unpaired mappings, or interchangeability across a broad range of model pairs.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Compares several criteria for ranking alignment placements, including CKA, Gram similarity and readout R². Does not systematically vary neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.

Shows incomplete recovery of teacher increments and a deep-layer stall, but does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause this pattern, nor test convergence across independently trained models generally.

rows.subject: SiT-B/2
rows.operation_detail: Linear readout of teacher increments from frozen student hidden states; reports the best readout across blocks and noise levels.
rows.measure: Held-out explained variance R² for the teacher-layer increment
rows.baseline: R² approximately 0 means a linear map finds none of the increment.
rows.note: The paper says the shallow increment is recovered early and its best readout remains near 0.2 through 400K steps.
rows.check: R² near 0.2 demonstrates incomplete recovery, despite the authors describing this shallow increment as filled early.

rows.subject: SiT-B/2

rows.measure: Held-out explained variance R² for the teacher-layer increment
rows.baseline: R² approximately 0 means a linear map finds none of the increment.
rows.note: The paper describes this as close to the readout floor.
rows.check: The authors describe deep-increment recovery as near the measurement floor and almost nonexistent through 400K steps. Absence of recovery supports V7's incompleteness component.

rows.subject: SiT-B/2
rows.operation_detail: Linear readout of the whole whitened teacher layer from the student.
rows.measure: Held-out explained variance R² for the whole teacher layer
rows.baseline: R² approximately 0 means a linear map finds none of the target.
rows.note: This is greater than the recovery of the layer-12 increment because the whole deep layer carries shallower content forward.
rows.check: Also bears on V7: whole-layer R² of 0.18 demonstrates substantial unrecovered representation even when inherited content is included.

rows.subject: SiT-B/2
rows.operation_detail: Measures the remaining recoverability gap at the selected teacher-layer/student-block cell after alignment.
rows.baseline: Unaligned run at the selected cell: 0.92
rows.note: Alignment reduces the gap but does not close it.
rows.check: Deliberately induced alignment is excluded from spontaneous-convergence verdicts. This is Table 3 row 4's ablation aligning layer 12 at block 6 until 250K, not the main RARE run.

rows.subject: SiT-B/2
rows.operation_detail: Measures the remaining recoverability gap at the selected teacher-layer/student-block cell after alignment and loss release.
rows.baseline: Unaligned run at the selected cell: 0.92
rows.note: The paper says the gap rises only to 0.64 after release, retaining most of the gap closed by alignment.
rows.check: Deliberately induced alignment is excluded. The measured run stops alignment at 250K, so 400K is 150K steps after release; the stated 154K release belongs to main RARE.
